column1: Severe bleeding in road accident (rural highway)
column2: How do I control severe bleeding from a traffic accident?
column3: Make area safe, put on gloves or use a clean cloth, apply firm pressure. Keep wound raised. Use a pressure bandage if available. Call for emergency help immediately.
column4: Kenya Red Cross 1199 (ambulance); Police 999/112; E-plus 0700 395 395

column2: If someone is bitten by a snake in the field, what should I do?
column3: Keep the person calm and still. Immobilize bitten limb at or below heart level. Do not cut or suck the wound. Quickly call emergency services or E-plus. Remove tight items from limb.
column4: Snakebite Hotline EMKF 0732 429 940; Ambulance 1199; Hospital local

column2: What’s the best way to treat a burn from hot water or open fire?
column3: Remove from heat. Cool burn under clean, cool running water for at least 10-20 minutes. Cover loosely with clean, non-adhesive cloth. Do not apply creams, and don’t pop blisters. Get help for severe burns.
column4: Ambulance 1199 (Kenya Red Cross); Local hospital; E-plus 0700 395 395

column2: How do I help a child who’s choking and can’t breathe?
column3: If coughing, encourage to keep coughing. If cannot breathe, bend the child forward, give 5 firm back blows between shoulders. If needed, give 5 abdominal thrusts. Repeat. Call for ambulance if not relieved.
column4: Ambulance 1199; Local hospital/practitioner; St. John Ambulance 0724-418811

column1: Sudden collapse, not breathing (heart attack, CPR)
column2: What do I do if someone is found collapsed and isn’t breathing?
column3: Send for help immediately. Start CPR: 30 chest compressions, 2 rescue breaths if trained, keep going. Use AED if available. Ambulance must be called as soon as possible.
column4: Ambulance/Kenya Red Cross 1199; Nairobi Hospital 020 2845000; Mater Hospital 071 9073000

column2: What should be done for a child who has ingested pesticide in a home?
column3: Do not induce vomiting. Try to identify the substance, keep the child calm, quickly call Poisons Centre for guidance, take to hospital with the chemical packaging.
column4: Poisons Centre 0703 618 367; Ambulance 1199; Hospital local

column2: How do I treat a dog bite to prevent infection or rabies?
column3: Wash thoroughly with soap and running water. Cover with clean cloth, do not suture unless at hospital. Seek urgent medical care for all animal bites (rabies risk).
column4: Ambulance 1199; Local hospital; District Vet (if wild animal involved)

column2: Someone has collapsed and is unconscious, what action should I take?
column3: Check responsiveness, open airway, check breathing. Place in recovery position if breathing. If not, start CPR. Keep warm. Get emergency help or local transport to clinic.
column4: Ambulance 1199; Police 999/112; Local clinic/hospital

column2: How do I help someone with a severe allergy reaction (swelling, great difficulty breathing)?
column3: Remove trigger if possible, call emergency help. If they have an adrenaline auto-injector (e.g., Epipen), help use it. Lay person flat if dizzy, raise legs if faint. Get ambulance support fast.
column4: Ambulance 1199; Hospital local; Mater Hospital 071 9073000

column2: What are FAST signs of stroke and what first aid can I provide?
column3: Use FAST: Facial drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call ambulance. Lay person down, keep airway open, call for help immediately.
column4: Ambulance 1199; Nairobi Hospital 020 2845000; Police 999/112

column4: How do I help someone pulled from water who is unresponsive?
column5: Ensure scene safety. Remove from water quickly but safely. Open airway, check breathing. If not breathing, start CPR immediately. Keep warm and get to hospital for evaluation.

column2: What should I do if someone receives an electric shock?
column3: Do NOT touch the casualty while current flows. Switch off power at source if safe. Once power is off, check responsiveness and breathing. Treat burns, start CPR if not breathing and call for emergency help.
column4: Ambulance 1199; Kenya Power emergency line; Local hospital

column2: How do I recognise and treat heat exhaustion or heatstroke?
column3: Move person to shade, cool with wet cloths, give sips of oral rehydration if conscious. For suspected heatstroke (confusion, high temperature), cool rapidly and call emergency services immediately.
column4: Ambulance 1199; Local clinic/hospital; Ministry of Health advice

column2: How do I help a diabetic having a seizure or very low blood sugar?
column3: If responsive and able to swallow, give fast-acting sugar (juice/Glucose gel). If unconscious, do NOT give by mouth; place in recovery position and call ambulance. Get to hospital for glucose monitoring.
column4: Ambulance 1199; Local hospital; Diabetes Association clinics

column3: What immediate steps help control severe bleeding after childbirth?
column4: Massage uterus if trained, encourage breastfeeding to stimulate uterine contraction, place clean pad and apply firm pressure to bleeding site. Call emergency services immediately and arrange urgent transfer to hospital.
column5: Ambulance 1199; Kenyatta National Hospital; Local maternity facility

column2: What is first aid for someone with a severe asthma attack?
column3: Help person sit upright, use their reliever inhaler (4 puffs via spacer if available) repeating as needed. If no improvement or worsening, call ambulance immediately.
column4: Ambulance 1199; Local hospital respiratory unit; Nairobi Hospital

column2: How do I manage a limb with a suspected open fracture?
column3: Stop any bleeding with direct pressure, avoid moving the limb unnecessarily. Immobilize with splints if trained, cover exposed bone with sterile dressing, and get urgent transport to hospital.
column4: Ambulance 1199; Local trauma hospital; Moi/Kenyatta Referral Hospitals

column1: Head injury with vomiting or confusion (road crash fall)
column2: What should I do for head injury with vomiting or confusion?
column3: Keep airway open, monitor breathing and level of consciousness, do not remove helmet if motorcyclist unless necessary, call ambulance urgently and avoid giving food/drink.
column4: Ambulance 1199; Major referral hospital; Police 999/112

column2: How can I safely help someone having a seizure?
column3: Protect from injury, place cushion under head, do not restrain, do not force objects into mouth. Time the seizure; if over 5 minutes or repeating, call ambulance. Place in recovery position once breathing returns.
column4: Ambulance 1199; Local hospital neurology unit; Emergency services

column1: Chemical splash to eye or skin (farm/industry)
column2: What immediate action for chemical eye splash or skin exposure?
column3: Flush affected area with copious clean water for at least 15 minutes. Remove contaminated clothing. Seek urgent medical care and bring product container to hospital.
column4: Poisons Centre 0703 618 367; Ambulance 1199; Local hospital

column3: What first aid and contacts are important after a violent assault?
column4: Ensure safety first. Treat life-threatening bleeding and injuries, preserve evidence if possible, seek urgent medical care, report to police and contact local GBV support services.
column5: Police 999/112; GBV Hotline 1195; Nearest hospital/emergency department

column2: How to triage and give first aid at a multi-victim road crash?
column3: Ensure scene safety, call for multiple ambulances, triage casualties by severity (Catastrophic bleeding, airway, breathing, circulation), apply life-saving interventions and organise transport to hospital.
column4: Police 999/112; Ambulance 1199; Kenya Red Cross; County emergency coordination
